instructions: Bihar STET Paper 2 Computer Science practice mock test.

questions.question: A missing closing parenthesis is usually detected primarily during:
questions.explanation: The parser detects violations of grammatical structure.

questions.question: Microteaching is designed mainly to:

options.text: Practise a specific teaching skill in a scaled-down lesson

questions.explanation: Microteaching isolates a skill with a small group, short lesson and feedback.

questions.question: Preventive classroom management emphasizes:

options.text: Clear routines, engaging tasks and expectations established in advance
Waiting until disruption escalates before planning
Using punishment as the only strategy

questions.explanation: Preventive strategies reduce the likelihood of disruption before it occurs.

questions.question: A screen reader is an example of technology that:

options.text: Reads on-screen text aloud or presents it through accessible output
Improves a monitor's refresh rate only

questions.explanation: Screen readers help users access digital content through speech or braille output.

questions.question: Lossy compression reduces file size by:

options.text: Discarding some information that may be less perceptually important
Increasing the sample rate without changing data
Adding redundant copies of every pixel

questions.explanation: Lossy codecs trade exact reconstruction for smaller data sizes.

questions.question: An item that is too easy for nearly all candidates may still be useful when it:

options.text: Checks an essential prerequisite, even if it offers limited discrimination
Has no relation to the syllabus
Has two correct options without explanation

questions.explanation: Very easy items can verify foundational knowledge, though they may discriminate poorly.

questions.question: Method overloading is typically resolved using:

options.text: The method name and parameter signature at compile time
The runtime value of every local variable only

questions.explanation: Overload resolution generally uses the declared parameter types and applicable language rules.

questions.question: MQTT is commonly used for:

options.text: Lightweight publish-subscribe messaging in constrained or connected systems

questions.explanation: MQTT is a lightweight messaging protocol using a brokered publish-subscribe model.

questions.question: In immediate addressing, the operand value is:

options.text: Always stored in a stack frame
Fetched only from an I/O port

questions.explanation: Immediate mode embeds the operand value within the instruction encoding.

questions.question: DNS primarily translates:

options.text: Domain names into resource records such as IP addresses

questions.explanation: DNS resolves names to records, commonly including IP addresses.

questions.question: In CSS, which selector has the highest specificity among these?
questions.explanation: An ID selector generally outranks class and type selectors in specificity.

questions.question: A B+ tree index is especially useful because it:

options.text: Keeps keys ordered and supports efficient range queries
Stores all records only in CPU registers
Requires every search to scan all rows

questions.explanation: B+ trees support balanced searches and linked leaf-level range traversal.

questions.question: In C, an enumeration is used to define:

options.text: A set of named integer constants

questions.explanation: enum defines named integral constants.

questions.question: A strong primary defense against SQL injection is to:

options.text: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements
Concatenate raw user input into SQL

questions.explanation: Parameter binding keeps data separate from SQL syntax.

questions.question: A router primarily forwards packets based on:
questions.explanation: Routers use network-layer information and routing tables to select a next hop.

questions.question: Indexed file allocation stores file block addresses in:
questions.explanation: An index structure records the disk block pointers for a file.

questions.question: The zone of proximal development refers to tasks a learner can complete:

options.text: With guidance but not yet independently
Only after forgetting all prior knowledge
Without any learning or support ever
Only when the task is already mastered independently

questions.explanation: ZPD concerns the gap between independent performance and performance with assistance.

questions.question: Intrinsic motivation occurs when a learner engages in an activity mainly because:

options.text: The activity itself is interesting or satisfying
A prize is the only reason to participate

questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest or inherent satisfaction in the activity.

questions.question: Accurate attendance records help schools to:

options.text: Identify patterns and follow up on absences appropriately

questions.explanation: Attendance records support monitoring, safeguarding and timely intervention.

questions.question: Binary search requires the searched sequence to be:

options.text: Stored in a linked list only

questions.explanation: Binary search relies on a sorted or otherwise monotonic search space.

questions.question: Which Java block is intended to execute whether or not an exception is thrown, in ordinary control flow?
questions.explanation: A finally block is used for cleanup and generally executes as control leaves the try statement, with defined exceptions.

questions.question: Corrective software maintenance addresses:

options.text: New features caused by a changed business environment only
Porting to a new platform only
Code readability without any change request only

questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance fixes defects found in operational software.

questions.question: Which condition is one of the four Coffman conditions for deadlock?
questions.explanation: Circular wait is one of mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait.

questions.question: Which format is generally suitable for lossless raster image storage and supports transparency?
questions.explanation: PNG supports lossless compression and alpha transparency; JPEG is typically lossy.

questions.question: A Turing machine's tape is commonly modeled as:

options.text: An unbounded sequence of cells for the theoretical model
A network packet buffer of one byte

questions.explanation: The standard theoretical model uses an unbounded tape, though only finitely much is used in finite computation.

questions.question: A demonstration is particularly appropriate when learners need to:

options.text: Observe a process or procedure before practising it
Memorize an unrelated list of dates
Replace every hands-on activity with dictation

questions.explanation: Demonstration makes procedural steps visible before guided or independent practice.

questions.question: Thrashing occurs when a system spends excessive time:

options.text: Handling page faults and swapping pages rather than executing useful work
Running CPU instructions from cache only

questions.explanation: Thrashing is associated with a very high page-fault rate and insufficient resident memory.

questions.question: A context-free grammar has productions whose left-hand side is:

options.text: Any arbitrary string of terminals and nonterminals
An empty set of symbols in every rule

questions.explanation: In a CFG, each production has one nonterminal on the left-hand side.

questions.question: Which Python object is immutable?
questions.explanation: A tuple's item references cannot be reassigned after construction, though contained mutable objects can change.

questions.question: In `int main(int argc, char *argv[])`, `argc` conventionally represents:

options.text: The number of command-line arguments including the program name
The number of characters in argv[0]

questions.explanation: argc counts the argument strings, conventionally including the program name as argv[0].

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Madhya Pradesh among the listed options.

questions.question: Insertion sort performs especially well on:

options.text: Every reverse-sorted large array with O(1) time

questions.explanation: Insertion sort is adaptive and can run near-linearly on nearly sorted inputs.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is most closely associated with routing between networks?
questions.explanation: Layer 3, the Network layer, handles logical addressing and routing.

questions.question: A common way to reduce overfitting is to:

options.text: Use regularization or suitable validation-based model selection
Train indefinitely on the same data without checks
Evaluate only on the training set

questions.explanation: Regularization and validation help control model complexity and generalization.

questions.question: The mean of 4, 8, 10 and 14 is:
questions.explanation: The sum is 36 and 36/4 = 9.

questions.question: RFID systems commonly use radio waves to:
questions.explanation: RFID reads data from tags using radio-frequency communication.

questions.question: The principle of least privilege means users and processes should receive:

options.text: Only the permissions needed for their tasks
The same permissions regardless of role

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits access to what is necessary.

questions.question: A circular queue is useful because it:

options.text: Reuses freed positions at the front of a fixed-size array
Eliminates the need for front and rear indices
Supports access only to the middle element

questions.explanation: Circular indexing reuses array positions freed by dequeues.

questions.question: A local variable declared `static` inside a function retains its value:

options.text: Between calls for the lifetime of the program

questions.explanation: A block-scope static object has static storage duration.

questions.question: Which is a form of non-verbal communication?
questions.explanation: Facial expression communicates meaning without words.

questions.question: In a max-heap, each parent key is:
questions.explanation: A max-heap maintains parent ≥ child for every edge.

questions.question: Conflict serializability can be tested using a precedence graph; the schedule is conflict-serializable if the graph is:

options.text: A tree with exactly one node

questions.explanation: A cycle in the precedence graph indicates the schedule is not conflict-serializable.

questions.question: A left-recursive grammar can cause problems for a naive:

options.text: Bottom-up shift-reduce parser in every case

questions.explanation: Direct left recursion can lead to infinite recursion in naive recursive-descent parsing.

questions.question: The `volatile` qualifier tells the compiler that an object's value:

options.text: May change in ways not apparent from ordinary program flow

questions.explanation: volatile limits certain optimizations because the value may change externally; it does not itself guarantee atomicity.

questions.question: Accessing an array element by a valid index typically takes:
questions.explanation: Array indexing computes an address directly in constant time.

questions.question: Which clause handles a matching exception in Python?
questions.explanation: Python uses except clauses to handle exceptions.

questions.question: A file extension is primarily used to indicate:

options.text: A conventional file type or format

questions.explanation: Extensions commonly signal file type, though they do not guarantee actual content.

questions.question: ISRO is India's national agency primarily concerned with:
questions.explanation: ISRO leads India's space programme.

questions.question: A latch is generally described as:

options.text: A combinational circuit with no memory
A device that stores multiple bytes permanently

questions.explanation: A latch responds to an enable level, while a flip-flop is commonly edge-triggered.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to A + A'B?
questions.explanation: Using absorption, A + A'B = A + B.

questions.question: A teacher handling sensitive student records should:

options.text: Share them only with authorized people for legitimate purposes
Post them on a public noticeboard
Keep no safeguards because the records are educational

questions.explanation: Confidential information should be protected and disclosed only appropriately.

questions.question: Before using a digital simulation, a teacher should first check whether it:

options.text: Matches the learning objective and is accessible to the learners
Requires the newest device regardless of access

questions.explanation: The tool should fit the objective and learners' access needs.

questions.question: Differentiated instruction may vary tasks or supports based on:

options.text: Learner readiness, interests or learning needs while pursuing meaningful goals
A fixed assumption that ability never changes
Random assignment with no learning rationale

questions.explanation: Differentiation adapts routes and supports to learner needs.

questions.question: Fair treatment does not always mean identical treatment because:

options.text: Learners may need different supports to access the same learning goal
Every learner must receive the same feedback regardless of work

questions.explanation: Equity can require appropriate supports while preserving fair standards.

questions.question: Symmetric encryption uses:

options.text: A shared secret key for encryption and decryption
A public key only for both operations
A hash digest as a reversible key

questions.explanation: Symmetric schemes use shared secret key material.

questions.question: A TLB is used to cache:
questions.explanation: A Translation Lookaside Buffer speeds up address translation by caching page-table entries.

questions.question: Breadth-first search typically uses a:

options.text: Hash function as its sole data structure

questions.explanation: BFS explores vertices level by level using a queue.

questions.question: Which transport protocol is connectionless and does not itself guarantee delivery?
questions.explanation: UDP sends datagrams without TCP-style connection establishment or delivery guarantees.

questions.question: A Java class can directly implement:

options.text: No interfaces if it extends a class
An interface only if it has no methods

questions.explanation: Java classes can implement multiple interfaces, though they extend at most one class.

questions.question: A recursive function must have a valid way to:

options.text: Reach a terminating condition for intended inputs
Allocate a global variable on every call
Return a pointer in every case

questions.explanation: A base case or other terminating logic prevents unbounded recursion for supported inputs.

questions.question: Common subexpression elimination attempts to:

options.text: Reuse a previously computed expression when safe
Convert every variable into a global variable

questions.explanation: The optimization avoids recomputing equivalent expressions when intervening effects do not invalidate them.

questions.question: Responsible digital citizenship includes:

options.text: Respectful communication, privacy awareness and evaluating information
Posting other people's private data for entertainment
Assuming all online claims are true

questions.explanation: Digital citizenship combines safe, ethical and informed participation online.

questions.question: Which feedback is most actionable?

options.text: Your explanation states the claim; add evidence from the data in paragraph two
You are naturally bad at science

questions.explanation: Specific feedback links performance to a concrete next step.

questions.question: A candidate key is a minimal set of attributes that:

options.text: Must contain every attribute in the relation

questions.explanation: A candidate key is unique and minimal.

questions.question: Universal Design for Learning encourages multiple means of:
questions.explanation: UDL offers varied ways to engage, access information and demonstrate learning.

questions.question: Polymorphism allows:

options.text: A common interface to support different implementations or forms
Every class to contain exactly one method
All objects to have identical internal state
Methods to run without any object or function call

questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows uniform use of different implementations through a shared interface.

questions.question: A test of programming logic that mostly rewards handwriting quality has a concern with:
questions.explanation: Irrelevant handwriting demands may prevent the test from measuring programming logic cleanly.

questions.question: The enhanced greenhouse effect is mainly linked to increased atmospheric:
questions.explanation: Human-caused increases in greenhouse gases contribute to warming by trapping outgoing infrared radiation.

questions.question: A 4-bit binary counter can represent how many distinct states?
questions.explanation: Four bits represent 2^4 = 16 binary states.

questions.question: Direct Memory Access allows a device to:

options.text: Transfer data to or from memory with reduced CPU involvement
Execute every user program without an OS
Convert source code to machine code

questions.explanation: DMA controllers manage transfers while freeing the CPU from handling each data item.

questions.question: The HTML `<label>` element is primarily used to:

options.text: Associate descriptive text with a form control

questions.explanation: Labels improve form usability and accessibility by associating text with controls.

questions.question: Which function moves a file position indicator to a specified location?
questions.explanation: fseek changes the file position indicator for a stream.

questions.question: Which action can help conserve water at school?

options.text: Repairing leaks and using water efficiently
Washing paved areas with continuous running water

questions.explanation: Fixing leaks and reducing waste are practical water-conservation measures.

questions.question: For `a = [2,4,6,8,10]`, what is `a[1:4]`?
questions.explanation: Slicing includes index 1 and excludes index 4.

questions.question: A foreign key constraint primarily ensures that referenced values:

options.text: Match an eligible key in the referenced relation or satisfy the allowed NULL rule
Are always unique in the referencing table

questions.explanation: Referential integrity prevents invalid references to missing parent rows.

questions.question: Which cloud service model typically gives the customer control over deployed applications while the provider manages runtime infrastructure?
questions.explanation: PaaS generally provides a managed platform for deploying customer applications.

questions.question: Assessment reliability refers most directly to:

options.text: Consistency of scores across relevant repetitions, raters or items
Whether the test measures the intended construct
Whether the paper uses colour printing

questions.explanation: Reliability concerns consistency; validity concerns whether the intended construct is measured.

questions.question: A non-functional requirement can specify:

options.text: A particular user-visible business operation only
A test case's random seed only

questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements address qualities or constraints such as performance, reliability or security.

questions.question: Integrated circuits became a defining technology of which computer generation?
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers are associated with integrated circuits.

questions.question: A good account-security practice is to:

options.text: Use unique passwords and a reputable password manager where appropriate
Reuse one short password on every service

questions.explanation: Unique passwords limit damage from credential reuse; password managers can help maintain them.

questions.question: The pumping lemma for regular languages is commonly used to:

options.text: Show that certain languages are not regular
Determine the exact runtime of any program

questions.explanation: A contradiction with the pumping property can establish non-regularity.

questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 6, 12, 24, __.
questions.explanation: Each term is doubled; the next term is 48.

questions.question: A laser printer forms an image on paper using:

options.text: Liquid ink sprayed through nozzles only
A thermal ribbon in every model

questions.explanation: Laser printers use toner and electro-photographic imaging.

questions.question: Turnaround time is generally the interval from:

options.text: First CPU dispatch to first preemption only
The first page fault to its service only

questions.explanation: Turnaround time includes waiting and execution from arrival/submission to completion.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties are listed in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are in Part IVA, Article 51A.

questions.question: HTTP cookies are commonly used to:

options.text: Maintain state or preferences across otherwise stateless requests
Store server-side database tables inside HTML

questions.explanation: Cookies let servers and clients exchange small pieces of state or preference data.

questions.question: Constructivist learning emphasizes that learners:

options.text: Actively build understanding using prior knowledge and experience
Can learn only by repeating exact wording

questions.explanation: Constructivism highlights active meaning-making and the role of prior knowledge.

questions.question: A value rises from 80 to 100. The percentage increase is:
questions.explanation: The increase is 20; 20/80 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: A digital signature primarily provides evidence of:

options.text: Message integrity and signer authentication, and can support non-repudiation

questions.explanation: Digital signatures verify a signature against a public key and message digest; they do not encrypt the message by themselves.

questions.question: Photosynthesis uses light energy to help convert:

options.text: Carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen in the overall process
Oxygen and sugar into nitrogen only
Soil directly into oxygen without water

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis stores light energy in chemical energy in organic compounds.

questions.question: A norm-referenced score describes performance mainly relative to:
questions.explanation: Norm-referenced interpretation compares an individual's performance with a reference group.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is intended to retrieve a representation without requesting a state-changing action?
questions.explanation: GET is intended for retrieval and is defined as a safe method.

questions.question: Heat transfer through direct contact between particles is called:
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers thermal energy through interactions between neighboring particles.

questions.question: A greedy algorithm makes a choice that is:

options.text: Locally attractive at each step according to its strategy
Guaranteed optimal for every problem by definition
Based on exhaustive enumeration of all solutions

questions.explanation: Greedy methods make local choices; correctness requires a problem-specific proof.

questions.question: A cache hit occurs when:

options.text: The requested data is found in the cache
The CPU must fetch the data from disk every time

questions.explanation: A cache hit means the requested item is present in the cache.

questions.question: A productive parent-teacher conversation should be:

options.text: Specific, respectful and focused on the learner's progress and support
Based on blame and unverified assumptions

questions.explanation: Respectful evidence-based communication supports collaboration.

questions.question: Which clause filters groups after aggregate values are computed?
questions.explanation: HAVING applies conditions to groups, commonly using aggregate expressions.

questions.question: If CAT is coded as DBU by shifting each letter one step forward, DOG is coded as:
questions.explanation: D→E, O→P and G→H, so DOG becomes EPH.

questions.question: Which statement about parity bits is correct?

options.text: They can detect every possible number of bit errors
They can detect any odd number of bit flips but not every even number
They correct all two-bit errors automatically
They are used only for character encoding

questions.explanation: A simple parity bit detects odd-count bit errors, but an even number of flips may preserve parity.

questions.question: Flexible grouping means that groups are:

options.text: Changed according to the task, goal or learner needs
Permanent for the whole school year by ability label

questions.explanation: Flexible grouping changes as learning purposes and needs change.

questions.question: Inflation refers to:

options.text: A sustained rise in the general price level
A fall in every individual price
An increase in a country's land area
A rise in employment by definition

questions.explanation: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level, reducing purchasing power when incomes do not keep pace.

questions.question: Evaporation can occur:

options.text: At the surface of a liquid below its boiling point
Only when the liquid is frozen

questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the surface over a range of temperatures.

questions.question: Cloud elasticity refers to the ability to:

options.text: Provision and release resources as demand changes
Keep resources fixed regardless of load
Guarantee every application has zero latency

questions.explanation: Elastic systems adjust resources dynamically with workload needs.

questions.question: Signed integer overflow in standard C is generally:

options.text: A compile-time error in every case

questions.explanation: Signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C.

questions.question: Which task is a natural application of a stack?

options.text: Finding the minimum spanning tree by itself
Maintaining sorted order with binary search

questions.explanation: Stacks support last-in-first-out processing such as balanced-delimiter checking.

questions.question: The binary number 101101 equals which decimal value?
For an imbalanced binary classification task, precision is:
questions.explanation: Precision measures the fraction of predicted positives that are true positives.

questions.question: A compiler symbol table commonly records:

options.text: Identifier attributes such as type, scope and storage information
The screen dimensions of the user

questions.explanation: Symbol tables support semantic analysis and code generation by tracking identifiers.

questions.question: Separate chaining resolves hash collisions by:

options.text: Storing colliding entries in a collection associated with a bucket
Moving every key to the next array index permanently

questions.explanation: Separate chaining stores multiple entries per bucket, often in a linked list or similar structure.

questions.question: Retrieval practice means learners:

options.text: Actively recall information rather than only reread it
Read the same page continuously without trying to remember
Copy a complete answer while looking at it

questions.explanation: Retrieval strengthens recall by requiring learners to bring information to mind.

questions.question: On a typical IPv4 LAN, ARP is used to discover:

options.text: A link-layer address associated with a local IPv4 address
The domain name for a public IP
The route to every remote network
The TCP port of a web server

questions.explanation: ARP maps an IPv4 address to a link-layer address on the local network.

questions.question: Simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per year for 2 years is:
Active listening involves:

options.text: Attending carefully, clarifying and responding to what is said
Planning a reply while ignoring the speaker

questions.explanation: Active listening uses attention, clarification and responsive feedback.

questions.question: Wind turbines convert the kinetic energy of moving air into:
questions.explanation: Turbines convert wind energy into mechanical rotation and then electrical energy.

questions.question: A sprint in Scrum is:

options.text: A fixed-length iteration producing a usable increment
A final project sign-off meeting only
A permanent freeze on customer feedback

questions.explanation: A sprint is a timeboxed period for achieving a Sprint Goal and producing an increment.

questions.question: The Election Commission of India is responsible for conducting elections to:

options.text: Parliament and State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President
Only municipal wards in every state

questions.explanation: The ECI administers elections to Parliament, state legislatures, President and Vice-President; local body elections are handled by State Election Commissions.

questions.question: A group of four adjacent 1-cells in a Karnaugh map eliminates how many variables compared with individual minterms?
questions.explanation: Grouping 2^2 cells removes two varying variables from the product term.

questions.question: Statements: All laptops are computers. Some computers are portable. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
questions.explanation: The first statement directly guarantees that all laptops are computers; the overlap with portable items is unspecified.

questions.question: In a standard BST, an inorder traversal visits keys in:

options.text: Ascending order when the BST ordering invariant holds
Reverse insertion order in every case

questions.explanation: Inorder traversal of a valid BST visits keys in sorted order.

questions.question: In C, the result of `7 / 2` when both operands are int is:
questions.explanation: Integer division discards the fractional part for positive operands.

questions.question: Polling differs from interrupt-driven I/O because polling requires the CPU to:

options.text: Run a separate process for each bit

questions.explanation: Polling checks device status repeatedly, while interrupts notify the CPU when attention is needed.

questions.question: Which standard C function releases memory obtained from malloc/calloc/realloc?
questions.explanation: free releases a dynamically allocated block.

questions.question: An IPv6 address is how many bits long?
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.

questions.question: The recurrence T(n)=2T(n/2)+n has asymptotic solution:
questions.explanation: At each level the work is Θ(n), and there are Θ(log n) levels.

questions.question: A database view is generally:

options.text: A virtual table defined by a query
A mandatory physical copy of every source table

questions.explanation: A conventional view presents query results as a virtual table, though materialized views store results.

questions.question: Positive reinforcement involves:

options.text: Adding a consequence that increases a behavior's future likelihood
Removing a stimulus to decrease behavior
Applying a consequence that always reduces behavior
Ignoring a behavior in every situation

questions.explanation: Positive reinforcement adds a consequence following behavior that increases its future frequency.

questions.question: A 16-to-1 multiplexer needs how many select lines?
questions.explanation: The number of select lines is log2(16) = 4.

questions.question: Floyd-Warshall is used to compute:

options.text: The minimum element of an array only

questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall computes shortest paths between all vertex pairs.

questions.question: Java bytecode is executed by the:
questions.explanation: The Java Virtual Machine executes or compiles bytecode for the host platform.

questions.question: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of decimal 175?
questions.explanation: 175 = 10×16 + 15, giving AF in hexadecimal.

questions.question: In most expressions, an array name is converted to:

options.text: A pointer to its first element
A pointer to its last element
An integer equal to its length

questions.explanation: Array-to-pointer conversion commonly yields a pointer to the first element, with exceptions such as sizeof.

questions.question: A pipeline hazard caused by an instruction depending on a previous instruction's result is a:
questions.explanation: A data hazard arises from dependencies between instructions.

questions.question: A binary semaphore can commonly be used to provide:

options.text: Mutual exclusion for a critical section

questions.explanation: A binary semaphore can coordinate access to a shared resource.

questions.question: P is the class of decision problems solvable in:

options.text: Polynomial time by a deterministic algorithm
Polynomial time by a nondeterministic algorithm only

questions.explanation: P contains decision problems solvable in deterministic polynomial time.

questions.question: Testing individual functions or modules in isolation is usually called:
questions.explanation: Unit tests focus on small units such as functions, methods or modules.

questions.question: Ransomware commonly:

options.text: Encrypts or blocks access to data and demands payment
Only changes a file extension harmlessly

questions.explanation: Ransomware extorts victims by denying access to systems or data.

questions.question: In C, which operator has higher precedence?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than logical OR, assignment and comma.

questions.question: An analytic rubric differs from a holistic rubric because it:

options.text: Scores separate dimensions or criteria individually
Is used only for multiple-choice tests

questions.explanation: Analytic rubrics break performance into dimensions and score each criterion separately.

questions.question: An LMS is primarily used to:

options.text: Organize learning content, activities, submissions and progress
Route internet packets between autonomous systems

questions.explanation: Learning management systems support course delivery, communication and tracking.

questions.question: A well-structured digital document supports accessibility by using:

options.text: Meaningful headings and logical reading order
Only visual position and colour to convey structure
Scanned images of text with no alternative

questions.explanation: Semantic headings and logical structure help screen-reader and keyboard users navigate content.

questions.question: Like magnetic poles:
questions.explanation: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

questions.question: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days.

questions.question: After asking a challenging question, a teacher should allow wait time so learners can:

options.text: Copy the answer from the board

questions.explanation: Wait time can improve response quality and broaden participation.

questions.question: Regular languages are closed under:
questions.explanation: Regular languages are closed under union, intersection, complement, concatenation and other operations.

questions.question: In a neural network, an activation function introduces:
questions.explanation: Without nonlinear activations, stacked linear layers collapse to a linear transformation.

questions.question: Which memory is generally closest to the CPU core and fastest among these?
questions.explanation: Registers are directly within the processor and are typically the fastest listed storage.

questions.question: Equivalence partitioning reduces test cases by:

options.text: Selecting representative inputs from classes expected to behave similarly

questions.explanation: Equivalence partitioning selects representative values from input classes.

questions.question: A subclass typically inherits:

options.text: Accessible members according to the language's inheritance and access rules
Every private implementation detail as directly accessible
The parent object's memory address permanently

questions.explanation: Inheritance reuses or specializes behavior, subject to access and language rules.

questions.question: A lesson objective should be aligned with:

options.text: The number of pages in a notebook

questions.explanation: Alignment connects intended learning, practice and evidence of achievement.

questions.question: Encapsulation is most directly supported by:

options.text: Bundling state with methods and controlling access to internal state
Replacing every class with a function

questions.explanation: Encapsulation groups data and behavior and exposes controlled interfaces.
